---
ast of Characters and Brief Bios
George Adamski (1891-1965): A Polish-born American citizen who became a prominent figure in early ufology, claiming to have had multiple contacts with extraterrestrials and publishing books and photographs purportedly documenting these encounters. He conducted world lecture tours, including the one in Australia in early 1959.
Jim Dobbs Jr.: A witness in Hobbs, New Mexico, who reported seeing a glowing egg-shaped object in February 1959.
Lee B. James (Lt. Col.): Chief of the Liaison Branch of the Army Ballistic Agency in Huntsville, Alabama. He commented on the potential implications of UFO sightings, particularly the Killian incident, during a talk in Detroit in February 1959.
George J. Dufek (Rear Admiral): A US Navy officer who commanded Operation Deepfreeze in Antarctica. In March 1959, he publicly stated his belief that it would be "very stupid" for humans to think they are the only intelligent beings in the universe, citing sightings reported by his team.
Albert Hunter (MP): A Member of Parliament in the UK who questioned the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation about the London Airport UFO sighting in March 1959.
John Hay (MP): The Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation in the UK who responded to questions about the London Airport UFO sighting in Parliament in March 1959.
Geoffrey de Freitas (MP): A Member of Parliament in the UK who asked the Secretary of State for Air about the London Airport UFO sighting in March 1959.
George Ward (MP): The Secretary of State for Air in the UK who responded to questions about the London Airport UFO sighting in Parliament in March 1959.
Percy Briggs: A driver in South Australia who, along with his passenger, reported seeing a large, dome-shaped UFO with colored lights in March 1959.
C. Towill: The Claypans Postmaster in South Australia who was a passenger with Percy Briggs and witnessed the UFO sighting in March 1959.
Cornelis Kolff: President of the Dutch Aeronautical Association who reportedly found Queen Juliana of the Netherlands to be very interested in George Adamski's UFO presentation.
Haye Schaper (Lt. Gen.): Chief of Staff of the Royal Netherlands Air Force who reportedly dismissed George Adamski as a "pathological case" after his presentation to Queen Juliana.
Queen Juliana (1909-2004): The Queen of the Netherlands who showed "extraordinary interest" in George Adamski's lecture on UFOs in 1959.
Antonio Sanchez: One of two men in Argentina who reported seeing a saucer-shaped object on the ground in May 1959.
Ernesto Fogliani: The other of the two men in Argentina who reported seeing a saucer-shaped object on the ground in May 1959.
Edward J. Ruppelt (Captain, USAF): Former head of Project Blue Book. In late May 1959, he communicated with Donald Keyhoe about revising his book on UFOs and indicated a neutral stance on the phenomenon.
Donald E. Keyhoe (Major, USMC, Ret.): A prominent ufologist and director of the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP). He corresponded with Ruppelt about his book revision and urged him not to retract his earlier views under pressure.
Fritz Zwicky (1898-1974): A Swiss astronomer whose reputation was mistakenly believed by some students to be under attack by George Adamski during his lectures in Switzerland in May 1959.
Otis T. Carr: A contactee and head of OTC Enterprises who was barred from selling stock due to fraud allegations by the SEC in May 1959.
Lari Kendrick: An employee of OTC Enterprises who was also barred from selling stock.
Charles O. Rhoades: Another employee of OTC Enterprises involved in the stock selling allegations.
Wayne Aho: An associate of Otis T. Carr who escaped arraignment in the stock fraud case.
Norman Colton: Another associate of Otis T. Carr who fled the state and could not be located in relation to the fraud allegations.
Charles S. Sheldon II: Technical director of the House Science and Astronautics Committee who communicated with NICAP in June 1959, stating UFOs did not pose a national security threat.
Richard H. Hall: A key figure in NICAP who received correspondence from Charles S. Sheldon II.
Alberto Perego: A diplomat who met with George Adamski in Rome in June 1959.
Mario Maioli: Another individual who met with George Adamski in Rome.
Rev. William Booth Gill (Father Gill): An Anglican missionary in Papua New Guinea who, along with many others, reported observing multiple UFOs and apparent occupants in late June 1959.
Napau Abednego (Mrs.): An indigenous person on Prince of Wales Island, Australia, who witnessed a large, glowing red object land in July 1959.
George Wilson (Captain): Pilot of a Pan American Boeing Stratocruiser who reported seeing a large bright light and satellite lights over the Pacific Ocean in July 1959.
Richard Lorenzen: Copilot on Capt. George Wilson's Pan American flight who also witnessed the UFOs.
Bob Scott: Flight Engineer on Capt. George Wilson's Pan American flight who also witnessed the UFOs.
Eileen Moreland: A farmwoman in Blenheim, New Zealand, who had a close encounter with a large object and observed figures inside in July 1959.
Larry Godwin: A resident of Salisbury, North Carolina, who experienced a flash of light, noise, and TV failure in July 1959.
Ray Stanford: An individual in Corpus Christi, Texas, who filmed cigar-shaped UFOs in July 1959.
Stan Seers: President of the Queensland Flying Saucer Research Bureau (QFSRB) in Australia who was contacted and infiltrated by an ASIO agent in August 1959.
Waveney Girvan: Became the editor of Flying Saucer Review in September 1959.
Brinsley Le Poer Trench (1911-1995): The previous editor of Flying Saucer Review who resigned in September 1959.
Giuseppe Cocconi (1914-2008): An Italian physicist who, with Philip Morrison, proposed the use of the 21 cm hydrogen line for interstellar communication detection in September 1959.
Philip Morrison (1915-2005): An American physicist who co-authored the paper on using the 21 cm hydrogen line for interstellar communication.
Henry Murray (1893-1988): A Harvard University psychologist who began controversial stress experiments on undergraduates in September 1959.
Ted Kaczynski (1942-2023): A Harvard undergraduate who was a subject in Henry Murray's stress experiments and later became known as the Unabomber.
Alston Chase: Author of Harvard and the Unabomber, which connected Ted Kaczynski's experiences in Murray's experiments to his later actions.
Walter E. Ogden: A rural mail carrier in Kentucky who reported seeing a glowing object that left a scorched ring in September 1959.
Thomas S. Power (General): Commander-in-Chief of Strategic Air Command (CINCSAC) who declared the first Atlas-D ICBM operational in September 1959.
Robert Dickerson: A police officer in Redmond, Oregon, who observed a bright light hovering near the airport in September 1959.
Joseph Alsop (1910-1989): A syndicated columnist who discussed classified intelligence about Soviet missile strength in October 1959.
Joseph Rogers (Maj., USAF): An Air Force officer who achieved a high airspeed in a Convair F-106 Delta Dart in December 1959.
Lorentz Johnsen: A witness in Norway who saw a dark object explode and fall into the water in late December 1959.
Kenneth Lindsley Jr.: A witness near Modesto, California, who saw a bright orange bowl-shaped object in December 1959.
Estelle Hendershott: A resident of Modesto, California, who also saw a bright object in the sky in December 1959.
Richard E. O'Keefe (Maj. Gen.): Acting inspector general of the Air Force who issued instructions about UFOs being "Serious Business" in December 1959.
Wilbert B. Smith (1910-1962): A Canadian engineer and ufologist who edited the Topside newsletter for the Ottawa Flying Saucer Club starting in March 1960.
Esse Jansson: A photographer in Sweden who photographed unidentified objects, possibly satellites, in March 1960.
Robert Filler (Captain, USAF): A pilot based at Travis AFB, California, who was scrambled to intercept a radar target in the summer of 1961.
Phil Lee (Lieutenant, USAF): The other pilot scrambled with Robert Filler in the summer of 1961.
Glenn E. Bradley: A witness in Ohio who saw a group of metallic discs fly over his farm in the summer of 1961.
Giacomo Barra, Giuseppe Pordoi, Filippo Marin, Silvano Guardinfante: Witnesses in a motorboat off Savona, Italy, who saw an object emerge from the sea in June 1961.
Mrs. James W. Annis: A librarian in Pennsylvania who observed unusual aerial objects in June 1961.
Jaime de Miranda (Patrolman): A police officer in Brazil who investigated a UFO sighting on a highway in June 1961.
Astrogildo de Medeiros (Patrolman): The other police officer with Jaime de Miranda.
José Otavia Leite (Marshal): Another responder to the Brazilian UFO sighting.
José-Gregorio Darnaude y Rojas Marcos: A witness in Spain who had a close encounter with a luminous disc in June 1961.
Betty Hill (1919-2004): One of the central figures in the alleged Hill abduction case of September 1961, who reported experiencing vivid dreams of a UFO encounter.
Barney Hill (1922-1969): Betty's husband and the other central figure in the alleged abduction, who also reported the UFO encounter and recalled details under hypnosis.
Paul W. Henderson (Maj., USAF): An officer at Pease AFB who spoke with Betty Hill about her initial UFO report.
Emanoil Manoliu: The son of a prominent novelist in Romania who saw a disc-shaped light and found ground traces in the autumn of 1961.
Mihail Sadoveanu: Emanoil Manoliu's father and a well-known Romanian novelist.
Waldo J. Harris: A private pilot in Utah who had a close encounter with a hovering UFO in October 1961.
Jay Galbraith: An airport controller in Utah who also witnessed Waldo Harris's UFO sighting.
Russell M. Woods: An airport attendant in Utah who provided an altitude estimate for the UFO.
Douglas M. Crouch: Chief of criminal investigation at Hill AFB who forwarded the report on Waldo Harris's sighting to Wright-Patterson AFB.
Allen Dulles (1893-1969): Director of Central Intelligence who resigned in September 1961.
John A. McCone (1902-1991): Allen Dulles's successor as Director of Central Intelligence.
Robert S. McNamara (1916-2009): Secretary of Defense who requested the creation of the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA).
Jamie Farr (born 1934): An actor who, with his wife, reported seeing a UFO in Arizona in 1962.
Joy Ann Farr: Jamie Farr's wife who also witnessed the UFO.
Donald Menzel (1898-1976): A Harvard astronomer and UFO skeptic whose book Flying Saucers was translated and published in Russia in 1962.
René Fouéré: Co-founder of the Groupe d'Étude des Phénomènes Aériens (GEPA) in France in 1962.
Françine Fouéré: Co-founder of GEPA.
Lionel-Max Chassin (1902-1970): Retired French army officer who became president of GEPA in 1964.
Paul Misraki (1908-1998) (as Paul Thomas): French composer who wrote a book linking UFOs to ancient myths in 1962.
Richard M. Bissell Jr. (1909-1994): CIA official who left his position in February 1962.
Richard Helms (1913-2002): Replaced Richard Bissell Jr. at the CIA in February 1962.
William T. Coleman (Maj., USAF): Pentagon UFO spokesman who was replaced in February 1962.
Carl R. Hart (Maj., USAF): Replaced William T. Coleman as Pentagon UFO spokesman in February 1962.
Roscoe Hillenkoetter (Vice-Admiral, USN, Ret.): Resigned from NICAP in February 1962.
Alec Birch: A 14-year-old in England who took a photo of alleged UFOs in February 1962, later admitting it was a hoax.
Ronald Wildman: A witness in the UK who encountered an unusual object that affected his car in February 1962.
Francis Gary Powers (1929-1977): CIA U-2 pilot who was exchanged for a Soviet spy in February 1962.
Rudolf Abel (1903-1971): Soviet spy who was exchanged for Francis Gary Powers.
John Glenn (born 1921): Astronaut who became the first American to orbit the earth in February 1962.
Leon Davidson (1922-2014): Chemical engineer who theorized about CIA UFO disinformation in Saucer News in March 1962.
Patrick J. Quirke: A psychiatrist who Betty and Barney Hill consulted in March 1962.
Duncan Stephens: A psychiatrist who the Hills consulted and who ruled out simultaneous hallucination.
J. M. Lowery (Capt., USAF): An Air Force pilot who saw a cylindrical object moving at high speed in Germany in March 1962.
Robert Friend (Lt. Col., USAF): Air Force officer who accompanied J. Allen Hynek to investigate the April 1962 meteor event.
Eladio M. Vázquez (Rear Adm.): Argentine Navy officer who observed a UFO in May 1962.
Aldo Molinari (Capt.): Argentine Navy officer who also witnessed the UFO with Rear Adm. Vázquez.
Luis Sanchez Moreno (Navy Capt.): Chief of intelligence at the Puerto Belgrano Naval Base in Argentina who interviewed witnesses of a UFO landing in May 1962.
Elizabeth Scott: A witness in Florida who saw a cigar-shaped object hovering in May 1962.
Miguel Thomé: An Argentine reporter who photographed a luminous object in May 1962.
Gordon Pendleton (Capt.): Pilot of an Aer Lingus airliner who saw a globe-shaped object in May 1962.
J. P. Murphy: First Officer on Capt. Pendleton's flight.
Rodolfo César Galdos (Lt.): Argentine Navy flight instructor who observed UFOs with a formation of planes in May 1962.
Roberto Wilkinson: A student pilot whose plane was trailed by a luminous object in May 1962.
Gloria Lee (1917-1962): A contactee who claimed to receive channeled messages and died during a fast for peace in December 1962.
J.W.: Gloria Lee's alleged space contact.
William H. Byrd: Gloria Lee's husband.
Nada-Yolanda (Pauline Sharpe): A medium who claimed to channel post-mortem messages from Gloria Lee.
Thomas M. Comella (as Peter Kor): Writer who proposed a non-extraterrestrial origin for UFOs in September 1962.
Robert Michael White (Maj., USAF): X-15 pilot who saw an object during a high-altitude flight in July 1962.
C. T. Loftus and H. Wilbert: Fishermen off New Jersey who saw unusual lights in July 1962.
Marvin Miles: Reporter who covered the sighting of a possible submarine off Catalina Island in July 1962.
Mr. and Mrs. M. O. Barton: A family in Mississippi who saw a bright object maneuvering in July 1962.
Rivalino Mafra da Silva: A diamond prospector in Brazil who reported encounters with small beings in August 1962.
Raimundo Mafra da Silva: Rivalino's son who witnessed some of the alleged encounters.
Wilson Lisbõa (Lt.): Chief of police in Diamantina, Brazil, who investigated Rivalino Mafra da Silva's claims.
Ann Druffel: A witness in California who observed an unusual cloud formation in August 1962.
Aileen Cummings: The other witness with Ann Druffel.
Geraldo Bichara: A soldier in Brazil who claimed to have been paralyzed by a light beam and later recalled an abduction under hypnosis in August 1962.
Walter T. Jones Jr.: A witness in Pennsylvania who saw a triangular formation of lights in August 1962.
Charles Brew: A farmer in Australia who, with his son, observed a unusual rotating object in February 1963.
Trevor Brew: Charles Brew's son who also witnessed the object.
Rute de Souza: A young girl in Brazil who saw an object crash into a river in October 1963.
Tetsuo Ioshigawa: A fisherman who also witnessed the object crashing into the river.
Nikolai Kardashev: Soviet astrophysicist who proposed the Kardashev scale for classifying civilizations.
Hayden C. Hewes: Founder of Interplanetary Intelligence of Unidentified Flying Objects.
Robert L. Stephens (Col., USAF): Pilot who set a speed record in a Lockheed YF-12A in May 1965.
Daniel Andre: Fire control officer who accompanied Robert L. Stephens.
Jacques Vallée: Systems analyst who published Anatomy of a Phenomenon in June 1965.
Mrs. J. Whitehead: A witness in the UK who saw a disc-shaped object with "windows" in June 1965.
James McDivitt (Gen., USAF, Ret.): Astronaut on Gemini 4 who spotted an unidentified object and took photos in June 1965.
Ed White (Maj., USAF): McDivitt's partner on Gemini 4, who was asleep during the sighting.
James Oberg: Flight controller at Johnson Space Center who offered an explanation for the Gemini 4 object.
Jorge Stanich: Meteorological officer in Antarctica who observed lights in June 1965.
Uladislao Duran Martinez (Cpl.): Garrison member in Antarctica who took photos of a UFO in July 1965.
Connie Wolferd: A witness in Pennsylvania who saw a clam-shaped object in July 1965.
Laura de Freitas Machado Fernandes: A witness in Portugal who saw a luminous red object in July 1965.
Manuel Fernandes: Laura's husband who also witnessed the object.
Denis Crowe: An aircraft artist in Australia who encountered a glowing disc on a beach in July 1965.
Carlos Videla Zamudio (or Zamandio): A civil engineer in Chile who saw a red object in July 1965.
Lieut. Anspaugh: An officer at Francis E. Warren AFB who logged UFO reports in August 1965.
John R. Lang (T/Sgt.): Watch supervisor at Tinker AFB who observed objects in August 1965.
Robert Risser: Astronomer at the Kirkpatrick Planetarium who contradicted the Air Force's explanation for the August 1965 sightings.
John Shockley: Meteorologist at Wichita Municipal Airport who tracked radar blips in August 1965.
Ellis Pike: Assistant meteorologist with John Shockley.
Robert Campbell: News photographer in Texas who photographed a UFO in August 1965.
Peter McCollum: Chief of Police in Sherman, Texas, who assisted Robert Campbell.
Francis C. Jennings: Boeing aerospace engineer who saw discs hovering in Seattle in August 1965.
June Webb: A witness in Seattle who also saw a disc-shaped object in August 1965.
David Gibson: A witness in Iowa who saw a disc land and a small being in August 1965.
Jack D. Bond (Maj.): An Air Force officer who saw a UFO making erratic movements near Springfield, Ohio, in August 1965.
Leonard Chalupiak: A witness in Pennsylvania who saw a disc-shaped object and experienced physical effects in August 1965.
Bernard E. Finch: A witness in the UK who had an encounter involving a static charge in September 1965.
John Lockem (Constable): A police officer in South Africa who saw a UFO land and take off in September 1965.
Koos de Klerk (Constable): The other police officer with John Lockem.
J. B. Brits (Lt. Col.): District commandant of Pretoria North who commented on the South Africa UFO landing.
Heliodoro Carrión: A pilot in Spain who observed a large UFO in September 1965.
James F. Townsend: A radio announcer in Minnesota who encountered a rocket-like object and small entities in October 1965.
Ian Kinsey (Seaman): A witness at a Canadian Forces Base who saw a lighted object and a smaller UFO enter it in November 1965.
George Pedley: A banana grower in Australia who saw a UFO rising from a lagoon, leaving a "nest" in January 1966.
Albert Pennisi: Owner of the farmhouse near where George Pedley saw the UFO.
Maria Ruiz Torres: A witness in Madrid, Spain, who saw an object descending in February 1966.
Juan Jiminez Dias: Another witness in Madrid who saw a possible door open on the object.
José Luis Jordán Peña: A motorist in Madrid who claimed a close view of the UFO and later confessed to a hoax.
Antonio Ribera: A Spanish ufologist to whom Jordán Peña sent a sketch of the UFO.
George Hunt Williamson (1926-1986): A contactee who reported seeing UFOs in Key West, Florida, in March 1966.
William E. 'Eddie' Laxson: A civilian instructor in Oklahoma who encountered a wingless aircraft on the road in March 1966.
C. W. Anderson: A truck driver who was another witness to the object seen by William Laxson.
John T. King: A witness near Bangor, Maine, who had a close encounter with an elliptical object and fired at it in March 1966.
J. Allen Hynek (1910-1986): Astronomer and UFO consultant to Project Blue Book who investigated reports in Michigan in March 1966.
David Fitzpatrick (Deputy): A deputy who took a photograph during the Michigan UFO flap.
Sara Robechek and Jo Wilson: Hillsdale College students interviewed by Hynek.
William Van Horn: A witness in Hillsdale, Michigan, interviewed by Hynek.
